workflow: Code and docs in English, conversation in Finnish. cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo test + pnpm check before every commit; CI on windows-latest runs the same. Commit straight to main while the repo is single-author (public since 17.9.2026); the Atlas model changes go through a PR on the Atlas repo, then wrangler deploy of the MCP worker. A new decision enters the Atlas model first and is rendered into docs/adr/ by node scripts/adr-from-model.mjs. End a session by updating docs/CHANGELOG.md, docs/BUILD_INFO.json and, if a lesson was learned, docs/LESSONS.md; put the status to Atlas.

P7, decided by the owner 23.11.2026, before the rest of P7: the update model is (1) GitHub Releases, the NSIS installer run over the installed version, with the app's About showing its version and a button that opens the releases page in the browser, and (2) a winget package, its manifest made by the release CI (wingetcreate). The app never fetches anything for an update; an opt-in in-app check (Tauri updater) is not taken now and would need its own decision, being a second network path beside Explain. Enters the Atlas model as an ADR when P7 starts. P7 also needs: the Claude Code integration as a visible first-run step in the app (collectors to ~/.reviewglass/bin, statusLine and PostToolUse in settings.json with a backup, chaining an existing statusLine, an undo button) and the uninstaller calling the app to remove it; the collectors replaced on every upgrade; the toast identity through the installed shortcut's AppUserModelID, checked on an installed build; one version across tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml and package.json; a release workflow on a tag; signing (SignPath Foundation for open source, or Microsoft Artifact Signing if available to an individual in Finland) or the SmartScreen warning documented
